name: Cobscook Bay State Park
note: Recommended by Grok as one of the best campgrounds in Maine.  Many campsites are lakefront.  --AWH  It's a tidal bay, not a lake: wide mudflats at low tide. Whiting Bay Camping Area has large drive-in RV sites on the bay; the Broad Cove and Cobscook Point waterfront sites are walk-in tent. For 2026 the park says power is off on sites 1-27 for a mechanical issue; those sites stay open. --Claude

field_notes.Season: Campground closes at noon on October 15.
field_notes.Booking: Online reservations ran 5/18-9/13 in 2026; from 9/14 through the park's close all sites are first-come. Triangle sites on the map aren't reservable. Group sites by phone. Up to 14 nights per reservation. Call center 800-332-1501.
field_notes.Fees: $20 a night for a Maine resident, $30 for a non-resident. Fees are per site for up to 6 people. Reserving adds a non-refundable $5 processing fee for each night, not once per booking. 9% lodging tax on camping fees. The schedule lists no hookup rate for this park. Bureau of Parks and Lands fee schedule, read 2026-10-12 (the same table since at least April 2024).
field_notes.Sites: Map classes: S up to 20 ft, M up to 25, L up to 30, X up to 35, U over 35, T walk-in tent. Numbered to 125; many of the Broad Cove and Cobscook Point sites are T.

name: Carolina Hemlocks Recreation Area
note: Sites are arranged along the South Toe River in Pisgah National Forest; some RV sites have direct river access.  --AWH

field_notes.Season: Winter 2026-27: closed; the 2026 season ended October 31 and the 2027 season opens April 1.
field_notes.Booking: Run for the Forest Service by FIND Outdoors (formerly the Cradle of Forestry In America Interpretive Association), (828) 675-5509; 15 of the 35 sites are first-come. Gate hours 7 a.m.-10 p.m.; call ahead for a late arrival.
field_notes.Fees: Standard campsite $28; Interagency Senior/Access cardholders $14 (single standard site only).
field_notes.Sites: recreation.gov's catalog: 35 standard sites (20 reservable, 15 first-come); RV lengths mostly 30 ft, three at 35 ft; 10 pull-throughs. The operator's page says 31 campsites, some with river access.

name: SH001 Town Hill
note: Buchanan State Forest motorized roadside site SH001 Town Hill (Sideling Hill area), on Welsh Road 4.56 miles from Old Route 126: a secluded grass parking lot for one small camper or two vehicles with tents (listed back-in, up to 55 ft), with road noise from I-70. No water, hookups, toilets or trash service (carry in, carry out). Permit and reservation always required; district office 717-485-3148. --Claude

field_notes.Booking: A permit and reservation are always required, on the Pennsylvania State Parks and Forests reservation site or 888-PA-PARKS. Check-in and check-out 3 pm; campers must vacate for at least 48 hours before returning.
field_notes.Fees: State forest motorized roadside campsite (a DCNR state FOREST program, not a state park): $10/night PA residents, $15/night non-residents, reserved through ReserveAmerica; 7-night limit.
field_notes.Sites: A single roadside site, SH001 Town Hill (Sideling Hill loop), on Welsh Road 4.56 miles from Old Route 126 (Spade Road / Crystal Springs for the first few miles). A grass parking lot that 'can hold 1 small camper trailer or 2 vehicles with tents'; listed back-in, max vehicle length 55 ft, 55-ft grass driveway at a slight grade, partial shade.

name: CV008 Oak Trail
note: Buchanan State Forest roadside campsite CV008 Oak Trail, on Blankley Road near Oak Trail, Fairview Trail and the Martin Hill ATV trails. A large grass lot (holds 3 trailer campers) with fire ring, picnic tables and a hitching post; easy access but visible from the road. Back-in, max vehicle length 60 ft. No water, hookups or dump station. Dispersed campsite; no water body adjacent. --Claude

field_notes.Booking: Permit and reservation required, online or by calling 888-PA-PARKS. Check-in and check-out 3 pm; campers must vacate for at least 48 hours before returning.
field_notes.Fees: State forest motorized roadside campsite (a DCNR state FOREST program, not a state park): $10/night PA residents, $15/night non-residents, reserved through ReserveAmerica; 7-night limit.
field_notes.Sites: A single roadside site on Blankley Road near Oak Trail and the Martin Hill ATV trails: a grass lot that holds 3 trailer campers or 6 vehicles with tents, with fire ring, picnic tables and a hitching post. Back-in, max vehicle length 60 ft (site 120 x 120 ft, 185-ft gravel driveway).

name: Big Flat Parking Area
note: Michaux State Forest rustic camping area in the Big Flat parking lot off Birch Run Rd: nine signed sites (001A-001I), all pull-throughs listed for vehicles up to 45 ft, suitable for camping with horses. Non-flush toilet nearby; no water, hookups, dump or trash service (pack out). Reservation and permit required through the PA State Parks & Forests reservation system or 888-PA-PARKS (888-727-2757). Open in winter too (one of four Michaux sites kept open from the third Sunday after Thanksgiving to April 1; forest roads are not plowed). Campfires prohibited Mar 1-May 25. Michaux district office 717-352-2211. No water body adjacent. --Claude

field_notes.Fees: State forest motorized roadside campsite (a DCNR state FOREST program, not a state park): $10/night PA residents, $15/night non-residents, reserved through ReserveAmerica; 7-night limit.
field_notes.Sites: Nine State Forest Rustic sites (001A-001I) marked off within the gravel Big Flat parking area; every one is listed as a pull-through with a 45-ft max vehicle length. Suitable for camping with horses.

name: Michaux State Forest Campsite 009 Haunted Hollow
note: Michaux State Forest motorized roadside site 009 Haunted Hollow, on Ridge Road just before Middle Ridge Road: one back-in site in full sun, listed for vehicles up to 45 ft on a short gravel driveway. No water body adjacent; no water, hookups, toilets or trash service (carry in, carry out). Permit and reservation always required; district office 717-352-2211. Not one of the four Michaux sites DCNR keeps open in the winter season (third Sunday after Thanksgiving to April 1), though the booking site lists it open year round. --Claude

field_notes.Season: The two official pages disagree: the booking site lists this site 'Open year round', while DCNR's Michaux camping page says only four parking-lot sites (#1, #2, #21, #22) are available in the winter camping season, from the third Sunday after Thanksgiving to April 1, and 'All other campsites are closed'.
field_notes.Booking: A permit and reservation are always required, on the Pennsylvania State Parks and Forests reservation site or 888-PA-PARKS. Check-in and check-out 3 pm; campers must vacate for at least 48 hours before returning.
field_notes.Fees: State forest motorized roadside campsite (a DCNR state FOREST program, not a state park): $10/night PA residents, $15/night non-residents, reserved through ReserveAmerica; 7-night limit.
field_notes.Sites: A single roadside site, 009 Haunted Hollow (North loop), on Ridge Road just before Middle Ridge Road. Back-in, max vehicle length 45 ft, 31-ft gravel driveway at a slight grade, full sun.

name: Forbes State Forest Campsite 001 Laurel Mtn Division
note: Dispersed motorized campsite in Forbes State Forest; no water body adjacent.

field_notes.Season: Open April 2 to the last day of the regular rifle deer season (ReserveAmerica shows 'Open through Fri Dec 11 2026'); closed for winter, and forest roads are not plowed.
field_notes.Booking: A permit and reservation are always required; reserve online or at 888-PA-PARKS. Forbes asks campers to take no more than one permit a month. Check-in and check-out 3 pm; campers must vacate for at least 48 hours before returning.
field_notes.Fees: State forest motorized roadside campsite (a DCNR state FOREST program, not a state park): $10/night PA residents, $15/night non-residents, reserved through ReserveAmerica; 7-night limit.
field_notes.Sites: A single roadside site, 001, Laurel Mtn Division of Forbes State Forest, on J.E. Miller Road, 0.4 mile past the gate (off Laurel Summit Road from Route 30). Back-In, max vehicle length 30 ft; site pad 85 x 15 ft with a 300-ft gravel driveway, 20-ft overhead clearance. All equipment must fit on the site pad; no more than 2 vehicles.

name: Forbes State Forest Campsite 003 Braddock Division
note: Roadside campsite 003 (Braddock Division) on Kirby Road in Forbes State Forest. A small spring-fed pond is nearby, but the booking site puts the site more than 300 ft from any lake or stream. --Claude

field_notes.Season: Open April 2 to the last day of the regular rifle deer season (ReserveAmerica shows 'Open through Fri Dec 11 2026'); closed for winter, and forest roads are not plowed.
field_notes.Booking: A permit and reservation are always required; reserve online or at 888-PA-PARKS. Forbes asks campers to take no more than one permit a month. Check-in and check-out 3 pm; campers must vacate for at least 48 hours before returning.
field_notes.Fees: State forest motorized roadside campsite (a DCNR state FOREST program, not a state park): $10/night PA residents, $15/night non-residents, reserved through ReserveAmerica; 7-night limit.
field_notes.Sites: A single roadside site, 003, Braddock Division of Forbes State Forest, on Kirby Road, 0.9 mile from Skyline Drive (off Route 40). Pull-Through, max vehicle length 30 ft; site pad 125 x 15 ft with a 60-ft gravel driveway, slight grade, 20-ft overhead clearance, partial shade. All equipment must fit on the site pad; no more than 2 vehicles.

name: Moon Lake Recreation Area
note: Pinchot State Forest rustic camping area: 12 reservable sites in the Moon Lake Recreation Area off Moon Lake Road. A lake is nearby, but the sites are not lakefront. Only three sites list a max vehicle length of 30 ft or more (001 at 40 ft, 003 at 32, 007 at 30); the rest take 16-20 ft. Non-flush toilets; no water, hookups or dump station. Closed November 15 to April 1. --Claude

field_notes.Season: 'This site is closed for the winter season November 15th to April 1st.'
field_notes.Booking: Permit and reservation required, on the Pennsylvania State Parks and Forests reservation site or 888-PA-PARKS. Check-in and check-out 3 pm; after a stay campers must vacate for at least 48 hours before returning. $10 a night PA residents, $15 non-residents.
field_notes.Fees: State forest motorized roadside campsite (a DCNR state FOREST program, not a state park): $10/night PA residents, $15/night non-residents, reserved through ReserveAmerica; 7-night limit.
field_notes.Sites: 12 State Forest Rustic sites in the Moon Lake Recreation Area plus an organized-group site. All back-in; listed max vehicle lengths are 40 ft (site 001), 32 (003) and 30 (007), the other nine 16-20 ft.

name: 003 Sassafras Hill
note:
003 Sassafras Hill
Dispersed campsite on Sassafras Hill in Pinchot State Forest; no water body adjacent.

field_notes.Booking: Permit and reservation required, on the Pennsylvania State Parks and Forests reservation site or 888-PA-PARKS. The site is behind a locked gate off Sassafras Hill Road; gate instructions come with the confirmation. Check-in and check-out 3 pm; vacate at least 48 hours before returning. $10 a night PA residents, $15 non-residents.
field_notes.Fees: State forest motorized roadside campsite (a DCNR state FOREST program, not a state park): $10/night PA residents, $15/night non-residents, reserved through ReserveAmerica; 7-night limit.
field_notes.Sites: A single roadside site behind a locked gate off Sassafras Hill Road (Thornhurst Tract): gravel pull-through, max vehicle length 40 ft. 'This campsite is accessed by remote state forest dirt or gravel roads and may not be suitable for some low-clearance vehicles or large trailers.'

name: Delaware State Forest Campsite E011 Maple Run
note: Delaware State Forest motorized roadside site E011 Maple Run (Edgemere area), off PA 402 about 4 miles south of I-84, beside the Maple Run ATV and snowmobile trailhead parking area. Pull-in gravel driveway (75 ft) to a 20 x 30 ft site; the booking site lists no max vehicle length and files it as a tent site. No water frontage, water, hookups, toilets or trash service (carry in, carry out). Permit and reservation always required; district office 570-895-4000. --Claude

field_notes.Season: Open year round on the booking site; state forest roads are not plowed, so winter access is not guaranteed.
field_notes.Booking: A permit and reservation are always required, on the Pennsylvania State Parks and Forests reservation site or 888-PA-PARKS. Check-in and check-out 3 pm; campers must vacate for at least 48 hours before returning.
field_notes.Fees: State forest motorized roadside campsite (a DCNR state FOREST program, not a state park): $10/night PA residents, $15/night non-residents, reserved through ReserveAmerica; 7-night limit.
field_notes.Sites: A single roadside site, E011 Maple Run (Edgemere loop), off PA 402 about 4 miles south of I-84, directly connected to the Maple Run ATV and snowmobile trailhead and parking area. Pull-in on a 75-ft gravel driveway; the site itself is listed 20 x 30 ft, no max vehicle length is given, and the booking site files it under Tent Site only. Limited to 2 vehicles.

name: Delaware State Forest Campsite S006 Thunder Swamp
note: Delaware State Forest motorized roadside site S006 (Thunder Swamp, Snow Hill area) in forested upland along PA 402, about 8.9 miles north of US 209. One pull-in site on a long gravel driveway, partial shade. No water, hookups, toilets or trash service (carry in, carry out). Permit and reservation always required; district office 570-895-4000. --Claude

field_notes.Season: Open year round on the booking site; state forest roads are not plowed, so winter access is not guaranteed.
field_notes.Booking: A permit and reservation are always required, on the Pennsylvania State Parks and Forests reservation site or 888-PA-PARKS. Check-in and check-out 3 pm; campers must vacate for at least 48 hours before returning.
field_notes.Fees: State forest motorized roadside campsite (a DCNR state FOREST program, not a state park): $10/night PA residents, $15/night non-residents, reserved through ReserveAmerica; 7-night limit.
field_notes.Sites: A single roadside site, S006 Thunder Swamp (Snow Hill loop), along PA 402 about 8.9 miles north of US 209. Pull-in on a 210-ft gravel driveway at a slight grade; site 75 x 50 ft, partial shade, 15-ft overhead clearance. No max vehicle length is given, and the booking site files it under Tent Site only.

name: Delaware State Forest Campsite S001 Snow Hill
note: Delaware State Forest motorized roadside site S001 (Snow Hill area) in wooded upland on Laurel Run Road, about 2.8 miles north of PA 447. One shaded back-in site for vehicles up to 40 ft on a gravel driveway. No water, hookups, toilets or trash service (carry in, carry out). Permit and reservation always required; district office 570-895-4000. --Claude

field_notes.Season: Open year round on the booking site; state forest roads are not plowed, so winter access is not guaranteed.
field_notes.Booking: A permit and reservation are always required, on the Pennsylvania State Parks and Forests reservation site or 888-PA-PARKS. Check-in and check-out 3 pm; campers must vacate for at least 48 hours before returning.
field_notes.Fees: State forest motorized roadside campsite (a DCNR state FOREST program, not a state park): $10/night PA residents, $15/night non-residents, reserved through ReserveAmerica; 7-night limit.
field_notes.Sites: A single roadside site, S001 Snow Hill (Snow Hill loop), on Laurel Run Road about 2.8 miles north of PA 447 (1 mile south of Snow Hill Road). Back-in, max vehicle length 40 ft; site 110 x 40 ft, gravel driveway at a slight grade, shaded, 15-ft overhead clearance.

name: S005 Brodhead Creek, Snow Hill
note: Delaware State Forest motorized roadside site S005 (Snow Hill area) on Laurel Run Road about 0.9 mile north of PA 447, named for Brodhead Creek at the lowest elevation of the forest's roadside sites. One back-in site for vehicles up to 30 ft on a short grass driveway, full sun. No water, hookups, toilets or trash service (carry in, carry out). Permit and reservation always required; district office 570-895-4000. --Claude

field_notes.Season: Open year round on the booking site; state forest roads are not plowed, so winter access is not guaranteed.
field_notes.Booking: A permit and reservation are always required, on the Pennsylvania State Parks and Forests reservation site or 888-PA-PARKS. Check-in and check-out 3 pm; campers must vacate for at least 48 hours before returning.
field_notes.Fees: State forest motorized roadside campsite (a DCNR state FOREST program, not a state park): $10/night PA residents, $15/night non-residents, reserved through ReserveAmerica; 7-night limit.
field_notes.Sites: A single roadside site, S005 Brodhead Creek (Snow Hill loop), on Laurel Run Road about 0.9 mile north of PA 447. Back-in, max vehicle length 30 ft; site 100 x 30 ft with a 30-ft grass driveway at a slight grade, full sun, 15-ft overhead clearance.

name: Weiser State Forest (Port Clinton Tract)
note: Weiser State Forest's Port Clinton Tract, on Oaks Road off PA 61 north of Hamburg, in wooded upland: three drive-in motorized roadside sites (PC002-PC004) plus a hike-in and a walk-to group site, reserved through the Pennsylvania State Parks and Forests system. No water, hookups, toilets or trash service (carry in, carry out). Permit and reservation always required; district office 570-875-6450. --Claude

field_notes.Booking: A permit and reservation are always required, on the Pennsylvania State Parks and Forests reservation site or 888-PA-PARKS. Check-in and check-out 3 pm; campers must vacate for at least 48 hours before returning.
field_notes.Fees: State forest motorized roadside campsite (a DCNR state FOREST program, not a state park): $10/night PA residents, $15/night non-residents, reserved through ReserveAmerica; 7-night limit.
field_notes.Sites: The pin is on Weiser State Forest's Port Clinton Tract (Oaks Road off PA 61 north of Hamburg), which has three drive-in roadside sites: PC002 (pull-in, 81-ft gravel driveway, site 104 ft), PC003 (back-in, 50-ft driveway at a severe grade) and PC004 (back-in, 27-ft driveway). None lists a max vehicle length and all three are filed under Tent Site only. The tract also has PC001 (hike-in, tent only) and PCG001, a walk-to site recommended for group camping. Up to 10 people per site.

name: Rainbow Springs State Park Campground
note: The campground is on the Rainbow River at a separate facility a few miles from the headspring; the park says its swim area and launch are a substantial walk from the campsites. --Claude

field_notes.Booking: Reserve on the Florida State Parks reservations website (Reserve Florida) or at 800-326-3521.
field_notes.Fees: $37 a night for an RV: the $30 campsite fee plus Florida's $7 nightly utility fee for RVs (tent campers pay $30), plus tax and a $6.70 reservation fee per reservation. No out-of-state rate; Florida residents 65 and over get half off the campsite fee. Reserve Florida's rate line for the campground and Florida's fee page, read 2026-10-12.
field_notes.Sites: 39 RV sites on concrete pads in Loops A-C plus 7 hike-in tent-only sites (water and 110-volt electric; park beside them). Reserve Florida lists the RV sites at 47-103 ft, nearly all back-in, two pull-through. The campground is a separate facility a few miles from the headspring; its gate is always closed and the code is given by phone (352-465-8550) on the day of arrival only. Check-in 3 p.m. or later, no early check-in.

name: Hunting Island State Park
note:
The campground is within an easy walk of the beach, but not close enough to be considered waterfront.
Recommended in _Where_Should_We_Camp_Next?_ by Stephanie Puglisi.  To reserve a single night, call the campground directly within one week of arrival.  --AWH

field_notes.Booking: Booked on South Carolina State Parks' own reservation site or 1-866-345-7275, up to 13 months ahead. 'Most campsite reservations require at least a 2-night stay'; per the --AWH note, a single night can be booked by calling the park within a week of arrival. One reservation may be no longer than 14 nights. Same-day reservations must be made directly with the park (843-838-2011).
field_notes.Fees: $75-85 a night for a standard campsite. The price changes by site and night, higher on weekends and busy dates. No reservation fee and no out-of-state rate. Every bookable night on the park's reservation calendar for two weeks from 2026-10-13 and from 2027-06-15, read 2026-10-12.
field_notes.Sites: 102 standard sites with electric and water in two campgrounds at the north end of the park, plus 25 walk-in tent sites and a primitive group area. Some sites take RVs up to 40 ft, others up to 28 ft.

name: Amelia Wildlife Management Area
note: One of the best dispersed camping areas in VA (per tmbtent.com). Multiple parking areas, including one on the lake.  --AWH  DWR bars camping within 300 ft of a lake or boat ramp, so camp at the inland lots, not the lakeside one. --Claude

field_notes.Booking: Camping on a Virginia WMA needs a written camping authorization ($10, up to six people) from Go Outdoors Virginia or a license agent, which sets the trip's start and end dates; 14 nights at most. Only in previously cleared spots, and 'unlawful to camp within 300 feet of any lake or facility'. DWR: 'WMA roads are not suitable for long vehicles or trailers ... Some WMAs may not allow travel trailers or RVs.' Amelia lists 'Primitive Camping' among its recreational opportunities; 'Numerous parking lots exist to access the area, and a concrete boat ramp is available'. The 300-ft setback rules out camping beside Amelia Lake or the boat ramp. Spring turkey season is quota-hunt only on Amelia (opening day and the next 3 weeks), and the two shooting ranges are open September 1 - March 31.

name: Wilson's Riverfront RV Park
note: Several primitive RV sites right on the French Broad River.  --AWH Closest RV park to downtown Asheville, on the French Broad River Greenway (kayak or tube from the park). Helene (2024) took the bath house and most of the trees, and tent camping has ended. --Claude

field_notes.Booking: Book online through Campspot (the site's 'Reserve Now'); Good Sam / Military codes entered at checkout. Monthly sites by email. On the dates tried (Nov 2026, June 2027) Campspot listed the No Hookup Riverside type with no bookable sites.
field_notes.Fees: Operator's rates page: primitive riverside RV sites (26, 28, no hookups) $40; Hillside full hookup $60 ($360/week); Riverside full hookup $65 ($390/week); monthly $1,200. Campspot, read 2026-10-22 for 2026-11-10 and June 2027: Hillside $63 and Riverside $68 a night with Campspot's $3 booking fee folded in (so $60/$65); the No Hookup type showed $43-48 but no bookable sites.
field_notes.Sites: Concrete pads; more than half the sites directly on the French Broad River. Two riverside primitive RV sites (26 and 28) with no hookups, concrete, back-in. Campspot lists Full Hookup Riverside and Hillside types (max 45 ft).

name: Hardware River Wildlife Management Area
note: Camping is in parking areas, not confirmed to be directly on the Hardware River.

field_notes.Booking: Camping on a Virginia WMA needs a written camping authorization ($10, up to six people) from Go Outdoors Virginia or a license agent, which sets the trip's start and end dates; 14 nights at most. Only in previously cleared spots, and 'unlawful to camp within 300 feet of any lake or facility'. DWR: 'WMA roads are not suitable for long vehicles or trailers ... Some WMAs may not allow travel trailers or RVs.' Hardware River lists Primitive Camping among its activities; besides the James River boat-ramp lot (where the 300-ft rule bars camping) DWR names upland parking areas on Kidds Mill Road and at the end of Route 611; its page names no camping spot.

name: Bear Creek Lake State Park
note: The RV sites are in the Black Oak and Chestnut loops, away from the lake.  --Claude 2026-10-21

field_notes.Season: First Friday in March through the first Monday in December (opened 3/6 in 2026). Chestnut Loop is open through October 31; Black Oak Loop begins closing by the second week of November for the Lights at the Lake setup.
field_notes.Fees: $37 a night for a site with electric and water; $43 with full hookups (Virginia residents); non-residents $43 / $50. The full-hookup price is for site 42 only. Sites without hookups are $32 but take rigs only to 20 ft. The same price every night of the week. Plus tax and a $5 transaction fee. DCR's fee table (effective 2025-05-12), read 2026-10-12.
field_notes.Sites: Only 11 sites take RVs: RV 21, 24, 25, 28, 29, 30, 32, 34 (Black Oak) and 42, 44, 45 (Chestnut), to 35 ft COMBINED tow vehicle + trailer. The other E/W sites hold pop-ups/equipment to 20 ft; Acorn sites 4-13 are water-view tent-only sites without hookups and site 18 is a tent-only E/W site. Acorn is the only loop by the lake.

name: 1868 Fire Trail Rd
note: Orchard Parking/Camping Area, Thompson WMA.  Very close to Appalachian Trail.  Not very level.  This is the last camping area at the end of Fire Trail road which is a minimally-maintained narrow dirt road.  Accessible by most 2WD vehicles in good weather but overgrown tree branches may make it a tight squeeze, and rocks/ruts may make it questionable for vehicles with very low ground clearance.  --AWH

field_notes.Booking: Camping on a Virginia WMA needs a written camping authorization ($10, up to six people) from Go Outdoors Virginia or a license agent, which sets the trip's start and end dates; 14 nights at most. Only in previously cleared spots, and 'unlawful to camp within 300 feet of any lake or facility'. DWR: 'WMA roads are not suitable for long vehicles or trailers ... Some WMAs may not allow travel trailers or RVs.' Thompson lists 'Primitive Camping' among its recreational opportunities and 'Parking is provided in 11 designated parking areas'; its ridge-top tract is reached from Linden on Route 638 (Freezeland Road), continuing 'on the unimproved Fire Trail'.

name: 300 Fire Trail Rd
note: Ridge Parking/Camping Area, Thompson WMA.

field_notes.Booking: Camping on a Virginia WMA needs a written camping authorization ($10, up to six people) from Go Outdoors Virginia or a license agent, which sets the trip's start and end dates; 14 nights at most. Only in previously cleared spots, and 'unlawful to camp within 300 feet of any lake or facility'. DWR: 'WMA roads are not suitable for long vehicles or trailers ... Some WMAs may not allow travel trailers or RVs.' Thompson lists 'Primitive Camping' among its recreational opportunities and 'Parking is provided in 11 designated parking areas'; its ridge-top tract is reached from Linden on Route 638 (Freezeland Road), continuing 'on the unimproved Fire Trail'.

name: Silver Bell
note: White River NF (Aspen-Sopris RD) campground in the Maroon Bells Scenic Area, 5 mi southwest of Aspen on Maroon Creek Rd at ~8,460 ft, in aspen and spruce beside Maroon Creek with views up the valley. Campers drive in on a vehicle pass bought at the Maroon Bells Welcome Station. Of the 14 sites only 007 (30 ft) takes a 23-ft rig; 001 is 22 ft and the rest are tent or walk-to sites (recreation.gov, 2026-10-28). The scenic area is closed to inbound private vehicles 8 am-5 pm, May 22-Oct 18; neither the FS nor visitmaroonbells.com says whether campers are exempt. --Claude

field_notes.Booking: The two RV-capable sites (001, 007) and tent-only sites 005 and 006 are reservable on recreation.gov at least 4 days ahead; sites 2-4 and 8-14 (all tent or walk-to) are first-come, claimed at the Maroon Bells Welcome Station (staffed 7 a.m.-7 p.m.) on arrival day, and usually full before noon in summer and fall. 'Five day' stay limit (recreation.gov: 4 nights in a rolling 30 days). Reservations must check in at the Welcome Station within 24 hours or the site is forfeited. 2026 reservation season May 22 - Sept 30 (2027: May 28 - Sept 30). Check-out 11 a.m.
field_notes.Fees: $15 a site (2026 and 2027 peak seasons). A $10 car pass, collected at the Maroon Bells Welcome Station as you enter, is required on top of the camping fee. 8 people and two cars per site.
field_notes.Sites: Only two sites take an RV or trailer: 001 (RV/trailer 22 ft) and 007 (30 ft), both reservable. The other 12 are tent-only (005, 006, 008-010, 014) or walk-to tent sites (002-004, 011-013). All back-in.

name: Hither Hills State Park Campground
note: In the dunes along the Atlantic Ocean at the northern tip of Long Island.  --AWH  PEAK-SEASON MINIMUM: mid-June to mid-September (2027: June 18 - September 11, by area) reservations are 7 nights only, one per person per peak season. --Claude

field_notes.Booking: ReserveAmerica, up to 9 months ahead, same day included. Peak season (mid-June to mid-September; 2027: June 18 - September 11, by area) takes 7-night reservations only, starting on the loop's own Friday, Saturday or Sunday, and only ONE 7-night reservation per name, address, email or phone. Non-peak minimum 2 nights, maximum 14 continuous nights then 48 hours away. Where less than the minimum stay is open, those nights go to walk-ins, first come first served. Register by 9 pm. Permit holder must be 21+ and present; reservations are non-transferable.
field_notes.Fees: $33 a night, or $37 on a Friday, a Saturday or the night before a holiday, for New York residents; non-residents pay double ($66 / $74). Nothing is added on top: all 176 sites are plain campsites with no hookups, and the booking site charges every one the same. The $33 already contains New York's $3 flagship-campground charge, and it matches the state's fee table only with the $10 oceanfront charge included too. $7.25 reservation fee. Read 2026-10-12.
field_notes.Sites: ReserveAmerica lists 176 campsites (the park description says a 190-site campground); listed equipment lengths 20-40 ft (118 at 30 ft, 15 at 40 ft), every driveway back-in. The J Loop is tent-only, key-card entry, no generators.
